advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Distinguish a failed/unreadable read-back (`<unread>`) from a confirmed still-set value in the Q1a/Q1b verdict formatting so a read failure isn't reported as 'IGNORED (still set)'.
evidence: `_req` returns `(0, repr(exc))` on transport error (line 76) and `(status, raw-string)` on non-JSON bodies, so `body` need not be a dict; `"<unread>"` is truthy and yields the IGNORED verdict.
ticket 4b9e warns: earlier changes 'shipped merged, mutation-proven and wrong' on unverified behaviour — a misclassified verdict defeats the probe's purpose.
scripts/jira_dc_epic_link_clear_probe.py:144: after1 becomes the truthy string `"<unread>"` when the read-back body is not a dict
advisory.finding: A failed read-back GET produces after1/after2 = "<unread>", which is truthy, so the verdict is reported as "IGNORED (still set)" — conflating a transport/read-back failure with the platform having ignored the clear. The probe's entire value is the correctness of this verdict.
merged_from: The Q1b update-verb fallback is gated on `if after1:`, so a failed/unreadable Q1a read-back (after1 == "<unread>", truthy) will trigger the second clear attempt even though the fields-form outcome was never actually determined.
scenarios: Read-back GET after the clear PUT hits a transport error or returns a non-dict body; probe records 'IGNORED (still set)' though clear status is actually unknown.
advisory.suggested_fix: Treat the `<unread>` sentinel as an explicit UNKNOWN branch in the verdict string (and in the `if after1:` fallback guard) rather than collapsing it into the truthy 'still set' case.
